subject: Control plane / data plane separation matrix and egress playbook for ACME on-prem
messages:
From: Kevin Lewis <kevin.lewis@acme.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Network Team <acme-ops@acme.com>
Date: 2026-05-30 08:14 -0700
Subject: On-prem VPC: boundary mapping + egress constraints (inventory attached)

Hi team,

Thanks again for the call yesterday. As we start to line up our internal change window, ACME needs a concrete mapping of the control plane vs data plane boundaries for the Redwood private deployment, plus a short egress playbook we can hand to our network ops people. Our requirements in short: PCI scope minimization, no direct internet egress from inference hosts, and the ability to route telemetry to our central observability cluster in us-east-1 over an outbound proxy.

I've attached our network inventory (acme-network-inventory.xlsx) that lists VLANs, NAT gateways, and firewall owners. Key constraints:
- Most inference nodes live in VLAN 210 (inference-prod).
- Management/control traffic originates from VLAN 20 (ops-mgmt) and must be routed over a dedicated transit VLAN.
- We require HSM-backed key material; we can provide an on-prem HSM or route to our KMS via a private peering.

Do you have a short mapping matrix and a recommended egress pattern we can approve this week? Preferably something that fits our change window on 06/05.

Thanks,
Kevin
Kevin Lewis
Senior SRE — ACME Corp.

Attachment: acme-network-inventory.xlsx (11 KB)

Subject: Re: On-prem VPC: boundary mapping + egress constraints (inventory attached)

Kevin — thanks, got the inventory and the call notes. We'll put together a concise mapping matrix and an operational egress playbook you can hand to network ops.

High-level plan:
1) Draft a control-plane / data-plane separation matrix mapping IP ranges, ports, and allowed destinations per role.
2) Propose two egress options: outbound proxy (recommended) or controlled NAT with stateful firewall rules.
3) Produce a short runbook for failover and a stubbed ACL list for ACME's firewall team.

Questions to confirm before we draft:
- Can inference hosts reach the outbound proxy on TLS 443 only? Or do you need other TCP ports for telemetry?
- Do you prefer the KMS connection over private peering (VLAN transit) or a local HSM appliance?
- Is there an existing jump-host bastion in VLAN 20 for admin access, or do you want us to propose one?

I've attached a first-pass mapping PDF (controlplane-data-mapping-draft.pdf) with our assumptions. Will iterate once you confirm the three bullets above.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
Attachment: controlplane-data-mapping-draft.pdf (42 KB)

Kevin / Connor — quick technical notes after reviewing the inventory and the draft:

1) Egress pattern
- Outbound proxy is the least privileged approach: inference hosts only need to reach the proxy on 443, proxy performs TLS inspection and forwards to telemetry endpoints. This preserves PCI scope because you can network-segment inference hosts away from any direct internet egress.
- Controlled NAT works if ACME can enforce very tight outbound rules on the NAT gateway and ensure no admin tools allow arbitrary outbound connections. In practice that increases audit surface.

2) Control plane endpoints
- We recommend colocating Redwood control plane endpoints on a separate transit VLAN (proposed VLAN 30) with ACLs allowing ingress only from ops-mgmt VLAN 20 and the Redwood-managed control IPs. Data plane (inference) VLAN 210 should be isolated such that it cannot initiate control-plane reconfiguration to other management systems.

3) Telemetry and observability
- For metrics/traces going to us-east-1 please confirm if you prefer TLS to the observability endpoint over the outbound proxy or a dedicated peering to us-east. The proxy route is simpler for routing policy.

4) HSM/KMS
- If you provide an on-prem HSM, we will integrate with the HSM using the standard PKCS#11 flow. If not, private peering to your KMS is acceptable but requires persistent encrypted tunnels and an agreed SLA for key availability.

I'll add these notes to the draft and update the matrix. Connor — can you capture these as discrete action items in the playbook and include the minimal ACL examples?

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Kevin — quick compliance note here since you called out PCI:

- Any telemetry or logs that include cardholder data must never leave the PCI-scoped VLANs. If telemetry includes only application metrics (no PANs), routing through the outbound proxy is fine provided the proxy is documented in the PCI network diagram.
- For KMS/HSM: HSM on-prem is the preferred option to keep keys inside ACME scope; if using remote KMS via peering, we need a documented key custody model and proof of encrypted tunnels.

Connor / Irene — please add two checklist items to the egress playbook: 1) validate telemetry payloads for PCI artifacts prior to export, 2) include required SOC2 audit logs (token-level usage and model-version access) and where they will be stored.

Link to internal compliance checklist: https://drive.redwood.com/ops/compliance/pci-soc2-checklist (ACME can view if we share).

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Head of Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference

Kevin — thanks for the quick turnaround on answers in the thread. Attached is v1 of the "VPC egress playbook" (vpc-egress-playbook-v1.md) and an updated separation matrix embedded in the document. Summary of decisions / askables for ACME network ops:

Decisions taken (we'll operate under these for the 06/05 change window):
- Control-plane endpoints will be placed on transit VLAN 30. Only ops-mgmt VLAN 20 and Redwood control IPs allowed to initiate to ports 443 and 22.
- Data-plane (inference) hosts remain in VLAN 210; egress to the internet must go through the outbound proxy on 443. No direct NAT egress from VLAN 210 for external destinations other than the proxy.
- HSM: ACME will provide an on-prem appliance. Redwood to integrate via PKCS#11.
- Telemetry: routed via outbound proxy to us-east-1 observability cluster; confirm proxy TLS intercept policy.

Action items for ACME Network Ops:
- Share firewall ACL template (we provided a starter set in the playbook).
- Confirm change window 06/05 02:00–04:00 UTC and nominate a network lead who will do the ACL cutover.
- Provide contact and local HSM admin details for Redwood to test key integration.

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
